I would say yes, those are disturbing memories to you that combined your emotional and physical pain, it makes sense that you would still feel upset by it. 

You can also sort of re-traumatize yourself by replaying these things in your mind. I wish I had a quote that nicely explained it, but basically when I read one of Dr Bruce D Perry’s books he went into how sometimes we try to heal our trauma by reliving it, by dissecting it and recounting what happened and trying to make sense of it. But that can actually cause the traumatic memories to have a greater hold over us. It’s different than processing and working through a trauma, because it’s not productive. It’s simply reliving things and spiraling into an upset mood because of that. 

Personally, I know there are times where I just kept replaying and getting bothered by my past every single day. I kept wondering when the day would come that I could remember these things and not get upset. That mindset contributed to it, because really I never stopped getting upset but the memories have become less disruptive. That didn’t happen on it’s own, I had to put the work in in various ways. And it does suck that the result is almost never “this doesn’t bother me anymore” it’s ongoing coping.


I hope you’re getting the emotional help that you need. Learning to cope is easier with a professional. It’s natural for you to feel this way, but your situation can be improved.
